title: Larger Bore Flush Valve and Re-Routed Waste Line at the Rear Lavatories
abstract: A wider flush valve bore and a straighter run from the rear lavatories to the waste tank, aimed at the blockage and valve removal rate that short-sector operators see and long-sector operators do not.

sections.reason: A maintenance provider replaced forty-one flush valves in twelve months across twenty-six CIRRANE-13 aircraft, roughly four times the published unscheduled removal rate, with the removals biased strongly to the rear lavatory and to operators flying five or more sectors a day. Investigation found that the rear waste line has two tight bends within a metre of the bowl, and that on short sectors the line never sees a long enough transport event to clear them. The valve itself is not failing: it is being commanded against a partly blocked line and its seat is being damaged. A revised servicing instruction issued in 2024 did not change the numbers.
sections.description: The flush valve bore is increased from 38 mm to 48 mm and the first metre of the rear waste line is re-routed with a single 45 degree bend instead of the two 90 degree bends it now has. The bowl latch D3830113615277 is replaced to suit the larger valve flange, the lower retaining latch D3830119707579 is repositioned, and the floor cover D3830119251732 is re-cut for the revised line path. Protective sleeving AES710749-83 is applied where the line passes the seat track. The waste partition 7WP and the lavatory partition 804WM keep their identifiers but the aft one is trimmed by 12 mm at the lower corner. Revised detail is on drawings D38300053631 and D38300000012. Work is done in the rear lavatories and the space behind them, zones 941, 943 and 945.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 0.6 kg per aircraft because the shorter line and the deleted bend outweigh the heavier valve. No electrical load change. The valve is not interchangeable with the current item because the flange bore differs, and a mixed installation between the two rear lavatories is not permitted since they share a line. Water and waste servicing is unchanged, and the water servicing panel is not touched. Illustrated parts content for the lavatory and the removal and installation tasks for the toilet assembly all need re-issue.
sections.embodiment_note: Launched in September 2025 with a production cut-in planned once the line routing is validated on a delivered aircraft. Retrofit is a two-shift task with the rear lavatory monuments removed, so it is scheduled with a cabin visit rather than offered as a night-stop task.
sections.open_points: The first pre-analysis round found that the re-routed line crosses the area used by an existing repair scheme on the aft floor structure, so a second round has been raised to close that point, together with the question of whether the trimmed partition still meets the flammability substantiation and whether the cabin lining standard fitted to later aircraft clears the new line path.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in planned after the line routing is validated on a delivered aircraft
